Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Civic life: news, government & the law

influence noun and verb

power over what others think and do

also have influence, influential, sway, carry weight, be influenced by, clout, have a lot of influence with

classical

Cic. Lael. 13: plūs apud mē antīquōrum auctōritās valet
Caes. BG 1.3.1: auctōritāte … permōtī

auctōritās, auctōritātis f.

noun, third declension

influence, weight, prestige: the standing that makes others follow

Lewis & Short: “might, power, authority, reputation, dignity, influence, weight (very freq.)”. It counts with someone: auctōritās valet apud aliquem.

Other words

  • grātia, grātiae f. — influence won by favour and connections

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Caes. BG 7.63.1: quantum grātiā, auctōritāte, pecūniā valent; Caes. BG 1.9.3: grātiā et largītiōne … plūrimum poterat

    Lewis & Short: “credit, influence”.

  • multum posse (valēre) apud — have great influence with

    phrase: apud with the accusative of those influenced; plūs, plūrimum for more and most · also used · classical · Caes. BG 1.9.3: plūrimum poterat; Cic. Lael. 13: plūs apud mē … valet; Traupman 101: multum posse in (+ abl.)

    The usual way to say that someone has influence: how much he can do, or how much he counts, with others.

  • addūcō, addūcere, addūxī, adductum — influence, induce (someone to act)

    verb, third conjugation; with ut and the subjunctive, or ad · also used · classical · Caes. BG 1.3.1: hīs rēbus adductī … cōnstituērunt

    In the passive, of the reasons that move someone: hīs rēbus adductus, influenced by these considerations.

  • flectō, flectere, flexī, flexum — sway, bend (someone’s mind or will)

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Hor. Ars 163: cēreus in vitium flectī; Cic. Phil. 1.35: sed quid tē ōrātiōne flectam? (Lewis & Short)

    Lewis & Short: “to bend (in opinion or in will), to move, persuade, prevail upon”.

Examples

  • plūs apud mē antīquōrum auctōritās valet

    the authority of the ancients carries more weight with meCic. Lael. 13

  • Hīs rēbus adductī et auctōritāte … permōtī cōnstituērunt ea quae ad proficīscendum pertinērent comparāre

    Influenced by these considerations and moved by (Orgetorix’s) authority, they decided to get ready what they needed for the journeyCaes. BG 1.3.1

  • quantum grātiā, auctōritāte, pecūniā valent, ad sollicitandās cīvitātēs nītuntur

    with all the influence, authority and money they have, they set about stirring up the statesCaes. BG 7.63.1

  • inberbus juvenis tandem custōde remōtō gaudet equīs canibusque et aprīcī grāmine Campī, cēreus in vitium flectī, monitōribus asper

    the beardless youth, his tutor gone at last, delights in horses and hounds and the grass of the sunny Campus: soft as wax to be shaped to vice, rough with those who advise himHor. Ars 161–163

See also effect, important, factor, control.
